title: LGBTQ Influencer Mad Sandhu Shot Dead in Amritsar, Sparking Punjab Law-and-Order Row
excerpt: Mad Sandhu, a makeup artist with 2.26 lakh Instagram followers, was gunned down by two motorcycle-borne men on Saturday evening; the BJP and Congress blamed the AAP government's law-and-order record as police said they had leads.
body:
• Makeup artist and LGBTQ influencer Mad Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was shot dead by two motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar around 6 pm on Saturday. He was rushed to Fortis Hospital, where he died during treatment.
  • Police have registered an FIR based on the family's statement and say they are working multiple angles; the motive behind the killing is not yet known.
  • The BJP and Congress blamed the AAP government's law-and-order record. MP Tarun Chugh called the killing "extremely tragic and heart-wrenching" and said Punjab had been turned into a "crime capital," while Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka said law and order had "completely collapsed."
  • Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had spoken about them openly on social media.

Mad Sandhu, a makeup artist and one of Punjab's most visible LGBTQ influencers, was shot dead by two men on a motorcycle in Amritsar on Saturday evening, a killing that has set off a fierce political battle over law and order under Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's Aam Aadmi Party government.

Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was attacked on Loharka Road around 6 pm while waiting at a car wash for his car. Two to three rounds were fired, one eyewitness said at point-blank range. He was taken to Fortis Hospital in critical condition and died during treatment; a video of the aftermath has circulated widely on social media.

Police say they have leads; motive unknown

Police registered an FIR on the basis of statements recorded from Sandhu's family and began the preliminary investigation on Saturday night. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sirivennela said officers had some leads and would arrest the accused soon. "Two unidentified men fired at him around 6 pm," he said.

DCP (Investigation) Prabhjot Singh Virk told reporters the probe was in its initial stages and that police were working on multiple angles. The motive for the killing had not been established, and investigators had not determined whether Sandhu's public profile, personal disputes, or some other factor was connected to the attack.

"God has made me the way I am."

— Mad Sandhu, speaking about the homophobic abuse he faced online

Opposition turns the heat on the AAP government

The killing drew swift condemnation from the BJP and the Congress, both of which accuse the Mann government of presiding over a collapse in law and order. BJP MP Tarun Chugh called the daylight murder "extremely tragic and heart-wrenching," saying Punjab had been "handed over to criminals and mafias" and turned into a "crime capital" through Mann's "political failures."

Delhi BJP leader and minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said law and order was "in the hands of the mafia." Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka accused the government of sleeping while law and order had "completely collapsed," contrasting its publicity hoardings with what he called a "dishonest government." Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had spoken about them openly on social media. Verka added that neither Mann nor AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal had commented on the killing.

"This incident has once again exposed the shortcomings of the AAP government and proven that Punjab has been handed over to criminals and mafias, where the youth of Punjab are not safe."

— Tarun Chugh, BJP MP

Who was Mad Sandhu

Sandhu was born to a retired Punjab Police inspector and built his career in fashion as a stylist and assistant costume designer on productions in Punjab and Mumbai before expanding into social media. He founded the Mane Lane Unisex Salon in Amritsar and ran beauty academies training students in self and bridal makeup. His Instagram account had about 2.26 lakh followers, and he acted in the Punjabi film Oye Bhole Oye.

Openly gay, Sandhu spoke frequently on podcasts and digital platforms about gender, sexuality, makeup and the film industry, and was known for content on fashion, lifestyle and LGBTQ acceptance. He regularly faced homophobic abuse online but refused to hide his identity. A few months ago, a Nihang Sikh publicly objected to his social media content and clothing, saying it would have a negative impact on young people.

Why this matters for the diaspora

Punjab's large overseas community in Canada, the UK and the US follows law-and-order developments back home closely, given family ties, property and travel. The killing also feeds a wider diaspora conversation about visibility and safety for LGBTQ people in Punjabi society.

What happens next

Police say arrests will follow soon, but with no motive established the investigation could run in several directions — from personal disputes to the threats Sandhu himself had spoken about online. Politically, the opposition is expected to keep pressing the Mann government over drugs and gang activity in the border state.
